Title: Arabic-first correspondence
Decision: For Saudi/GCC bilingual business correspondence Arabic leads and English follows. Latin technical identifiers, filenames, URLs, codes and system references stay Latin/LTR. The GEM logo is never mirrored.
Effective scope: Correspondence only. It does NOT broaden S07 beyond its existing wayfinding scope.
Remaining evidence: Native Arabic linguistic review (44-item queue); continuous production RTL layouts; screen-reader order; AC10 Brand Owner decision.
Source / authority: Brand Owner instruction in the OD01 task brief, 2026-10-09. No individual name, signature or time was supplied; none is invented.

Title: Accessibility title policy
Decision: Every slide needing semantic navigation should have a meaningful accessibility title. Remediation must not alter approved visible geometry merely to satisfy a native checker. Use an existing visible heading where it can safely serve; otherwise a non-visible structural title only if visually neutral, semantically accurate and geometry-neutral. Title wording that needs interpretation is provided or approved by the Accessibility Content Owner.
Effective scope: Future title remediation in Parts A-D candidates.
Remaining evidence: 30 unresolved slide titles still need an owner disposition; assistive-technology testing.
Source / authority: Brand Owner instruction in the OD01 task brief, 2026-10-09. No individual name, signature or time was supplied; none is invented.

Title: Alt-text ownership
Decision: Informative imagery gets concise, meaningful alt text written or approved by the Accessibility Content Owner. Decorative, redundant, background and ornamental assets are marked decorative where supported. Generic filler descriptions that add no information are not acceptable.
Effective scope: All informative imagery in Parts A-D candidates.
Remaining evidence: 23 Part D product-image alt-text items, 6 generic Part D alt texts and 89 unclassified shapes still need an owner disposition.
Source / authority: Brand Owner instruction in the OD01 task brief, 2026-10-09. No individual name, signature or time was supplied; none is invented.

Title: Reading order
Decision: Final semantic reading order is validated manually through assistive-technology review. PowerPoint z-order or heuristic checker output is not changed in bulk without evidence that the resulting order is correct and visually safe.
Effective scope: Reading-order handling for Parts A-D candidates.
Remaining evidence: Manual assistive-technology review (200 heuristic-flagged slides and 7 Arabic/bilingual slides); screen-reader test matrix (13 scenarios) not run.
Source / authority: Brand Owner instruction in the OD01 task brief, 2026-10-09. No individual name, signature or time was supplied; none is invented.

Title: Contrast
Decision: The approved GEM palette is unchanged. Beige #BCACA7 on White #FFFFFF is not used for functional small text or other text needing WCAG AA contrast. The pairing may remain in palette specimens, demonstrations, decorative contexts and non-essential visual uses. The palette itself is not inferred to need change.
Effective scope: Palette-use policy. Treats the Beige-on-White pair on Part A slide 33 (a specimen candidate) as a policy matter.
Remaining evidence: Contrast of 113 text runs over pictures (manual); formal exceptions; confirmation that Part A slide 33 is a specimen.
Source / authority: Brand Owner instruction in the OD01 task brief, 2026-10-09. No individual name, signature or time was supplied; none is invented.

Title: Arabic / bilingual footer localization
Decision: Functional labels in Arabic and bilingual correspondence, including page labels where relevant, are localized appropriately. Tagline treatment follows the formally approved bilingual brand-language rule. No Arabic translation counts as linguistically approved until native Arabic linguistic review is complete.
Effective scope: Arabic and bilingual correspondence footers and functional labels.
Remaining evidence: Native Arabic linguistic sign-off of every localized label and the tagline translation.
Source / authority: Brand Owner instruction in the OD01 task brief, 2026-10-09. No individual name, signature or time was supplied; none is invented.

Title: Latin technical IDs
Decision: Technical identifiers stay in original Latin/LTR form inside Arabic and bilingual content. Latin language metadata is used where technically appropriate. Inter may be used for Latin technical identifiers only if it can be introduced without disrupting native layout, bidi behavior stays correct and native validation confirms it; otherwise the validated existing typography is preserved. No unnecessary mixed-script changes are forced.
Effective scope: Latin technical identifiers within Arabic and bilingual content.
Remaining evidence: Native validation of any Inter introduction; font licence and build verification (Y03, VAL-05).
Source / authority: Brand Owner instruction in the OD01 task brief, 2026-10-09. No individual name, signature or time was supplied; none is invented.

Title: Word section direction
Decision: Section-level RTL is not forced for consistency where paragraph- and run-level bidi settings already give correct native behavior. Section direction changes only when native Microsoft Word evidence shows a functional issue.
Remaining evidence: Windows Word and Word Online validation; multi-page continuation flow with real content.
Source / authority: Brand Owner instruction in the OD01 task brief, 2026-10-09. No individual name, signature or time was supplied; none is invented.

Title: Repository / Legal-IP visibility policy
Decision: Owner label: 'C — CURRENT PUBLIC REPOSITORY APPROVED'. The current GEM repository may remain public; public visibility is approved for the current repository and future controlled project material. This is an owner decision, not a legal opinion. It is not evidence of trademark availability, logo-artwork ownership, font licences, image/model/property rights, third-party marks, supplier legal clauses or publication rights for every asset. Note: the label 'C' is the owner's; option C in the D7 package reads 'Make repository private' and was NOT selected (see 06).
Effective scope: mish3labdul/GEM (origin), as named by the D7 package. The second public repository mashaelalh/GEM is not covered by this record.
Affected gates: D7 (owner visibility decision only); VAL-03; VAL-04; VAL-05; VAL-06; Y01; Y02; Y03; Y04
Remaining evidence: All Legal/IP evidence stays open where the governing gates require it.
